newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MOTT CENTURY GIVES QUEENSLAND BIG LEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MOTT CENTURY GIVES QUEENSLAND BIG LEAD.

text.p: Queensland opener Matthew Mott took full advantage of a late call-up to score a century on Friday and put Queensland in a commanding position on the third day of their Sheffield Shield match against Victoria.

Mott, who came into the side as a late replacement for injured opener Trevor Barsby, played resolutely and made 150 as Queensland reached 355 for four at the end of the third day at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
His maiden first-class century enabled Queensland to build a lead of 393 runs. Victoria had been dismissed for 191 in their first innings on Thursday, with Queensland resuming on one without loss.
Mott, who eventually fell leg before wicket to Victoria captain Tony Dodemaide, shared a partnership of 180 for the third wicket with Jimmy Maher.
Maher scored 95 before he was bowled by paceman David Saker. Queensland captain Stuart Law was unbeaten on 45 at the close, with Geoff Foley five not out.
